summary_en: This study tests whether the time of day that PD-1 or PD-L1 immunotherapy is given affects outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer and in locally advanced, resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. Patients are randomly assigned to receive their infusion before 12:00 PM or after 3 PM, for 4 cycles or 2 cycles depending on the listed intervention, with follow-up for up to 2 years; the length of each cycle is not stated. The record does not name a primary outcome, but it says survival and treatment response will be collected from medical records (Phase 2).
summary_es: Este estudio evalúa si la hora del día en que se administra la inmunoterapia con PD-1 o PD-L1 afecta los resultados en el cáncer de pulmón de células no pequeñas y en el carcinoma de células escamosas de cabeza y cuello localmente avanzado y resecable. Los pacientes se asignan al azar a recibir la infusión antes de las 12:00 p. m. o después de las 3 p. m., durante 4 ciclos o 2 ciclos según la intervención indicada; la duración de cada ciclo no se indica, y el seguimiento es de hasta 2 años. El registro no nombra un resultado principal, pero indica que se recopilarán la supervivencia y la respuesta al tratamiento de los expedientes médicos (fase 2).
who_for: Adults 18 or older with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (cohort 1).
Adults 18 or older with resectable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (cohort 2).
Able to give written informed consent and to follow study procedures, in the investigator's judgment.
not_for: Currently using steroids (prednisone 10 mg or more, or equivalent) that cannot be stopped at least 7 days before standard treatment.
Prior PD-1, PD-L1 or CTLA4 immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment received less than 6 months before screening.
Currently taking part in another treatment clinical trial.
